description: JACL Milestone 5 — String System: Heap-interned strings (non-null-terminated, length-carrying), intern table with pointer-equality comparison, string builtins (concat, length, slice, index), string comparison, value-to-string coercion, and string interpolation end-to-end

userStories.title: Heap string type and intern table
userStories.description: As the runtime, I need a heap-allocated interned string type so that strings longer than 7 bytes can be represented and deduplicated via an arena-allocated intern table.
acceptanceCriteria: JaclHeapString struct defined: { uint32_t length; uint32_t hash; char data[]; } — flexible array member
String data is NOT null-terminated; length field is the sole source of truth for string size
JaclInternTable struct: hash table with open addressing or chaining, arena-allocated buckets
jacl_intern(arena, table, data, length) returns JaclVal with JACL_TAG_STRING (0x05) and pointer payload to JaclHeapString
Interning the same byte sequence twice returns the same pointer (pointer equality guaranteed)
Hash function: FNV-1a or similar, operating on (data, length) pair — does not rely on null terminator
Table resizes (rehashes) when load factor exceeds 0.75
All allocations (table buckets, JaclHeapString instances) go through the arena
jacl_is_heap_string(v) predicate returns true for JACL_TAG_STRING values
Unit tests: intern a string and intern same bytes again — verify pointer equality; intern different strings — verify different pointers; strings with embedded NUL bytes intern correctly
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Unified string access API
userStories.description: As the VM and builtins, I need a uniform API to work with any string value (inline or heap) without caring about the underlying representation.
acceptanceCriteria: jacl_string_len(JaclVal v) returns uint32_t length for both inline and heap strings
jacl_string_data(JaclVal v, char* buf, size_t buflen) copies string bytes into buf and returns actual length — dispatches on tag: inline extracts from payload, heap copies from JaclHeapString.data
jacl_is_string(JaclVal v) returns true for both JACL_TAG_INLINE_STRING and JACL_TAG_STRING

jacl_string_eq(JaclVal a, JaclVal b) implements representation-aware equality: inline vs inline uses bitwise comparison of tagged values; heap vs heap uses pointer comparison (interning guarantees correctness); cross-representation uses length check + memcmp
jacl_string_cmp(JaclVal a, JaclVal b) returns int for lexicographic ordering (negative/zero/positive), works across all representation combinations
Unit tests verify all combinations: short==short, long==long, short!=long, short<long ordering, cross-representation equality edge case
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Compiler support for heap string literals
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to emit heap-interned string constants for string literals longer than 7 bytes, removing the current hard error that rejects them.
acceptanceCriteria: Compiler holds a pointer to a JaclInternTable (passed in via compilation context or owned by it)
AST_LIT_STRING with length <= 7 still emits inline string constant via jacl_inline_string (unchanged behavior)
AST_LIT_STRING with length > 7 interns the string via jacl_intern and emits the resulting JACL_TAG_STRING value as a bytecode constant
The compile error 'string literal exceeds 7-byte inline limit' is removed
[print "hello world"] compiles and runs without error (previously rejected)
[def greeting "hello world"] [print $greeting] works end-to-end
String constants appearing multiple times in source share the same interned pointer
Unit tests verify short literals still inline, long literals intern correctly, duplicate long literals share pointer
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Print support for heap strings
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want print to display heap strings correctly so that I can see long string values.
acceptanceCriteria: [print "hello world this is a long string"] prints the full string without garbage or truncation
[print "short"] continues to work unchanged (inline strings)
Print handler extracts string data via the unified API (jacl_string_data or direct JaclHeapString.data pointer access with length)
No trailing garbage or null-terminator issues — heap strings are not null-terminated, print must use length
Tests verify printing short strings, long strings, and that output matches exactly
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: String equality and comparison in the VM
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want == < > to work on strings so that I can compare them in conditions and sorting.
acceptanceCriteria: [== "abc" "abc"] returns true (inline-to-inline, bitwise fast path)
[== "hello world" "hello world"] returns true (heap-to-heap, pointer fast path via interning)
[== "abc" "def"] returns false
[< "abc" "def"] returns true (lexicographic byte comparison)
[> "def" "abc"] returns true
[== "abc" 42] returns false (type mismatch is not an error, just false)
VM comparison opcodes (OP_EQ, OP_LT, OP_GT, OP_LE, OP_GE) dispatch to jacl_string_eq / jacl_string_cmp when one or both operands are strings
Existing numeric comparisons continue to work unchanged
Tests cover inline-inline, heap-heap, mixed-type, and ordering comparisons
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: String concatenation (OP_CONCAT and concat builtin)
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to concatenate strings so that I can build new strings from parts.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_CONCAT opcode added to OpCode enum: pops two string values from stack, pushes their concatenation
Concatenation result is inline (JACL_TAG_INLINE_STRING) if total length <= 7, otherwise heap-interned via the intern table
concat registered as a builtin command: [concat "hello" " world"] produces "hello world"
concat accepts 2+ arguments (variadic): [concat "a" "b" "c"] produces "abc" — compiler emits pairwise OP_CONCAT chain
Concatenating two empty strings returns empty inline string
Concatenating an inline string + heap string works correctly
VM has access to the intern table for creating heap-interned concatenation results
Tests verify short+short, short+long, long+long, variadic, and empty string cases
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: String builtins (length, slice, index)
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want string inspection operations so that I can query and extract parts of strings.
acceptanceCriteria: [length "hello"] returns i32(5)
[length ""] returns i32(0)
[length "hello world this is long"] returns correct length for heap string
[index "hello" 1] returns "e" (single-character inline string, 0-based indexing)
[index "hello" -1] or out-of-bounds index returns nil (not an error)
[slice "hello" 1 3] returns "el" (start inclusive, end exclusive)
[slice "hello" 2] returns "llo" (one-arg form: from start to end of string)
[slice "hello world this is long" 6 11] returns "world" (works on heap strings)
Slice result is inline if <= 7 bytes, otherwise heap-interned
All builtins work transparently on both inline and heap string inputs
Tests cover edge cases: empty string, full slice, zero-length slice, boundary indices
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: OP_TO_STRING value-to-string coercion
userStories.description: As the runtime, I need to convert non-string values to their string representation so that string interpolation can include numbers, booleans, and nil.
acceptanceCriteria: OP_TO_STRING opcode added to OpCode enum: pops a value, pushes its string representation
Integer to string: 42 becomes "42", -7 becomes "-7"
Float to string: 3.14 becomes "3.14" (reasonable formatting, no excessive trailing zeros)
Boolean to string: true becomes "true", false becomes "false"
Nil to string: becomes "nil"
String to string: no-op — already a string, pushed back unchanged
Closure to string: becomes "<proc name>" or "<closure>" (matches existing print type name behavior)
Result is inline if <= 7 bytes, otherwise heap-interned
Tests verify each type conversion produces correct string
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: String interpolation compilation
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want "hello $name, result is $[+ 1 2]" to produce a concatenated string at runtime, completing the interpolation pipeline from lexer through VM.
acceptanceCriteria: AST_INTERP_STRING compilation no longer errors — the stub 'interpolated strings not yet supported' is replaced with real compilation code
Each literal segment compiles to a string constant (inline if <= 7 bytes, heap-interned otherwise)
Each AST_VAR_REF segment compiles to: get variable value, then OP_TO_STRING
Each AST_COMMAND segment compiles to: compile the command expression, then OP_TO_STRING
Segments concatenated left-to-right using OP_CONCAT between each pair
[def name "world"] [print "hello $name"] prints 'hello world'
[def x 42] [print "x is $x"] prints 'x is 42'
[print "sum is $[+ 1 2]"] prints 'sum is 3'
[print "$[+ 1 2] plus $[+ 3 4]"] prints '3 plus 7'
Empty interpolation segments (adjacent interpolations) handled correctly without extra empty strings
Tests verify variable interpolation, expression interpolation, mixed segments, adjacent interpolations
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: End-to-end integration tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need comprehensive integration tests in test/test_m5.c exercising the full string system through jacl_run().
acceptanceCriteria: test/test_m5.c exists using jacl_run() and PrintCapture pattern from previous milestones
Test: [print "hello world"] prints 'hello world' (basic heap string literal)
Test: [def s "hello"] [print [concat $s " world"]] prints 'hello world'
Test: [print [length "hello"]] prints '5'
Test: [print [index "hello" 0]] prints 'h'
Test: [print [slice "hello world" 6 11]] prints 'world'
Test: [def name "JACL"] [print "hello $name"] prints 'hello JACL'
Test: [print "1 + 2 = $[+ 1 2]"] prints '1 + 2 = 3'
Test: [== "hello world" "hello world"] returns true via interned pointer equality
Test: [< "abc" "xyz"] returns true
Test: heap string used as proc argument and return value works correctly
Test: closure captures a heap string value
All existing M0-M4 tests continue to pass (build.sh full suite green)
Zero memory leaks detected by tracked allocator in all tests
Test file added to build.sh TESTS array
M5 row in DESIGN.md milestone table status updated from empty to **COMPLETE**
Commit message references M5 completion
